plans.prompt:
Create a production pixel-art animation sprite atlas of Cloud Strife from ORIGINAL FINAL FANTASY VII (1997), using the attached existing game sprites only as identity/style reference. He has sharply spiked golden hair, sleeveless dark purple SOLDIER outfit with loose purple trousers, brown boots, dark gloves, one steel left shoulder guard, and the enormous broad straight-edged grey BUSTER SWORD with its recognizable clipped tip and short red-brown hilt. No Remake harness redesign, no Fusion Sword, no gun, no extra weapons, no transformed outfit. Match the detailed crisp pixel sprite rendering of the reference. The character is a young adult with the same consistent proportions and costume in every cell. Transparent RGBA background, absolutely NO floor, horizon, grid lines, labels, captions, numbers, borders, or panel decoration. Native artwork only; each frame must actually change anatomy, limb bend, sword angle, and torso silhouette, never a translated duplicate or glow-only copy. All subjects stay fully inside their own equal cells with clear transparent gutters; every spike, hand, boot and sword tip is included. Face right throughout, allowing the torso to rotate naturally during an attack. Exactly FOUR columns: four sequential animation poses for each row, never a fifth figure. Frame positions must be evenly spaced. Each row is an independent state, not a continuation of the row above. Keep body scale consistent between rows; motions should read at small game scale. This is a generated 2D adaptation, not a claim of traced official frames.
Canvas portrait 1:2, ideally 1024x2048. EXACTLY EIGHT ROWS by FOUR COLUMNS, 32 full sprites total. Keep grounded soles at a common baseline within each ground-combat row. All attacks are physical sword techniques without lightning lasers or summoned creatures.
Row 1 attackLight1: quick rising diagonal Buster Sword cut. Four poses: low two-handed ready → sword sweeping diagonally upward before torso → high tip follow-through with arms extended → controlled high guard. Distinct knees and shoulder rotation.
Row 2 attackLight2: reverse horizontal cut. Four poses: torso wound back, sword high behind left shoulder → forceful rightward waist-height slash, right leg steps → broad blade extended far right and hips rotated → blade pulled back low with counter-rotation.
Row 3 attackLight3: stronger overhead finisher. Four poses: deep rear stance, both arms lift the heavy sword over head → downward blade mid swing in front of face → deep forward lunge with sword reaching ground level ahead → braced low finishing stance with bent front knee.
Row 4 crouchLight: low knee-bent sweeping sword cut. Four poses: crouched draw with left knee close to floor → compact rightward shin-height cut → blade extended to the right while body stays crouched → sword retracts into crouch guard. Never stand up in this row.
Row 5 chargeStart: physical windup. Four poses: standing sword guard → rear foot plants wider and knees bend → both hands lift sword behind head → whole body braced in a low charged stance, Buster Sword held back. The arms and sword change angle clearly in all four.
Row 6 chargeLoop: sustained physical bracing. Four poses cycle weight from rear foot → both knees deeper with hilt closer to shoulder → elbows widen and chest twists → rear heel braces and elbows draw in. Sword remains heavy and gripped with both hands. No energy ball; distinct real poses rather than identical idle art.
Row 7 chargeRelease: forceful two-handed diagonal cut. Four poses: deep windup with blade back → explosive forward hip turn and blade diagonally down across front → long full extension with leading leg bent and sword low ahead → heavy low follow-through. Only a small thin blade trail if needed, never obscuring the limbs.
Row 8 chargeRecovery: return after the heavy cut. Four poses: weight far forward and sword low ahead → rear leg steps under body as blade rises → torso straightens, elbows pull blade into guard → feet stabilize and sword returns to shoulder-height ready. Four different recovery postures.

Row 1 attackRecovery: after a normal sword strike. Four poses: forward bent stance with blade extended down-right → elbows retract the sword and lead knee bends → body rises, blade moves across torso → upright neutral guard with sword raised near shoulder. Clearly distinct recovery anatomy.
Row 2 special: CROSS-SLASH, the physical secondary limit technique, NOT Omnislash. Four poses: wide low stance and two-handed sword drawn back → first sharp diagonal sword cut down-right → reverse diagonal cut up-right with body rotation, forming a thin crossed slash trace → final horizontal cut and braced finishing lunge. No giant laser beam, no jumping Omnislash, no floating rune replacing the actual sword action. Only compact blade motion traces.
Row 3 aerialNeutral: airborne circular sword swing. Four poses: knees tucked while sword winds up at left → airborne torso twists and blade passes across front → blade follows round high-right while legs change tuck → knees open into falling-ready posture and sword returns near body. Every boot floats with no floor.
Row 4 aerialForward: airborne forward cleave. Four poses: raised sword behind head with both knees bent → chest twists right and both hands drive blade down-forward → sword reaches diagonally down-right with front leg opening → follow-through, tucked rear leg and torso recovering. Entire silhouette airborne.
Row 5 aerialDown: downward plunging Buster Sword attack. Four poses: knees tucked and sword raised → torso leans forward, sword rotates point-down below body → both hands guide point downward, legs spread back for balance → knees absorb imaginary landing as sword remains below hands, no ground painted. Sword points toward lower-right, not an energy projectile.
Row 6 intro: recognizable Cloud preparation. Four poses: sword tip down near side → both hands lift heavy Buster Sword in front → blade swings up and settles against shoulder → confident ready stance with one hand at hilt and free hand relaxed. No text or dialogue.
Row 7 victory: recognizable sword victory flourish. Four poses: broad blade raised in front → sword rotates across and above head with torso turn → blade lowered onto shoulder while other arm balances → relaxed upright sword-on-shoulder finish. Actual sword rotations and different arm positions.
Row 8 ledgeAttack: sword counterattack from hanging position, with NO ledge or scenery painted. Four poses: one gloved hand gripping invisible ledge at upper-right, body hangs beneath and Buster Sword points down from other hand → gripping elbow pulls torso toward imaginary edge, front knee tucks → torso rises above grip and free hand sweeps Buster Sword forward-right → crouched recovery on invisible platform at top of previous grip level, blade forward. Show the hand grip clearly and maintain consistent hypothetical edge position through the row.

Canvas portrait 4:5, ideally 1024x1280. EXACTLY FIVE ROWS by FOUR COLUMNS, 20 full sprites total. These are dedicated LEDGE MOVEMENTS, not standing combat poses. NO painted ledge, floor, rock, platform, boundary line or scenery anywhere. Infer an imaginary ledge just above and to the right of the hanging torso. Keep the invisible grip location near x=65% of each cell and y=20% of each cell. Make hands and grip readable; the hanging body and both boots are clearly below the grip. Buster Sword stays secured diagonally on his back except when hand placement changes during ascent; no extra sword, no fighting slash.
Row 1 ledgeCatch: four truly different airborne catching poses. Reaching right gloved hand upward toward invisible edge, knees trailing → fingers hook at imaginary edge, right arm fully stretched overhead, other arm reaches up → both hands grip at same edge, torso swings inward, knees tuck → elbows flex slightly, body settles into hanging posture and boots dangle. Grip fingers present, not holding sword above head.
Row 2 ledgeHang: four hanging poses beneath the same invisible grip point. Both hands hold overhead with elbows straight, knees loosely bent → left elbow bends and torso shifts toward edge, legs swing back → both elbows lengthen and knees draw forward → right elbow bends slightly as boots swing down. Each frame is truly suspended, shoulders below the grip, no standing.
Row 3 ledgeClimb: four distinct stages of pulling onto the invisible ledge. Both arms pull chest toward grip → elbows bend strongly and chin reaches edge level, right knee comes up → one palm presses down on edge as hips rotate and knee lifts over it → crouched body above former edge level with one hand braced below torso and Buster Sword still on back. Include entire figure within cell at every height; do not crop.
Row 4 ledgeDrop: four stages of release. Two-handed hang → one hand releases and body rotates slightly away → both hands release, arms lifted but open, body falls with bent knees → arms spread lower for balance, legs extend downward in freefall, entire body below old grip position.
Row 5 ledgeJump: four stages of jumping away from the edge. Hanging with both knees drawn up → arms push against the invisible edge and torso coils → fingers release, body launches upward-left with one knee raised and other leg extended back → airborne upward arc with both hands free and knees recovering. No ground-contact landing pose. All 20 figures remain complete and separate in their cells.
